chunks: Ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Ayyub from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:
Regarding a man upon whom was the fasting of two consecutive months for zihar, and he fasted Dhu al-Qa'dah, then Dhu al-Hijjah began for him, he said:

"He should fast the whole of Dhu al-Hijjah except the Days of Tashriq, then make them up on the first day of Muharram until he completes three days, so that he will have fasted two consecutive months."

He said: "It is not proper for him to approach his wife until he makes up the three Days of Tashriq that he did not fast. And there is no problem if he fasts one month and then fasts some days from the month that follows it, then an illness occurs to him causing him to interrupt them; then he may complete them afterward, after the completion of the two months."

key_terms.أَهْلَهُ: his wife/spouse, whom he should not approach before completing the required fast
key_terms.أَيَّامَ ٱلتَّشْرِيقِ: the Days of Tashriq during which fasting is excluded in this case
key_terms.شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ: two consecutive months required for kaffarah
key_terms.صَوْمُ: fasting; here, the expiatory fast obligation
key_terms.ظِهَارٍ: zihar, the pre-Islamic form of unlawful spousal declaration requiring expiation
key_terms.عِلَّةٌ: an illness or impediment that interrupts the fasting
key_terms.يَقْضِيهَا: he makes them up later as missed fast-days
key_terms.ٱلْمُحَرَّمِ: Muharram, the month in which the missed three days are made up

ai.seo_question: How is the fast of two consecutive months for zihar completed if the Days of Tashriq interrupt it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the kaffarah fast of two consecutive months in the case of zihar when the Days of Tashriq intervene during Dhu al-Hijjah. It explains that those prohibited days are excluded, then made up at the start of Muharram, and it also clarifies the ruling on resuming the fast if illness interrupts it after one month and some additional days have already been completed.
